cues.en: We think of the moon as orbiting the Earth following a spiraling trajectory as the Earth itself orbits the sun, but this is wrong. Not only is the moon's orbit not a spiral, there's an argument that the moon actually orbits the sun, not the Earth. Sure. From
cues.zh: 我们通常认为，月球沿螺旋轨迹绕地球运行，同时地球本身绕太阳运行，但这是错的。月球的轨道不仅不是螺旋线，还有观点认为月球其实绕太阳运行，而不是绕地球。当然。从

cues.en: perspective, the moon appears to orbit the earth, but from the sun's perspective or from an observer far above the solar system, the moon orbits the earth so slowly and the earth and moon are so far from the sun that the moon's trajectory never actually makes any sort of a loop. And in fact, it never even curves outwards towards the earth at all, but always inwards towards the sun. The moon's trajectory is more like a 12 sided polygon with curved corners than it is a spiral or even a wiggly line. Though the moon's trajectory is so close to being a circle, it's kind of hard to see. Here's a simpler example of an orbit where a planet's moon's trajectory only ever curves towards its sun. It looks like this hypothetical moon is actually orbiting the sun and just getting nudged in and out a little bit by the planet as it orbits. This type of curve where a circle rotates while attached to another rotating circle is called an
cues.zh: 视角来看，月球似乎绕地球运行；但从太阳的视角，或从太阳系上方很远处的观察者来看，月球绕地球转得太慢，而且地球和月球离太阳太远，以至于月球的轨迹其实从不形成任何闭合环路。事实上，它甚至从不向外朝地球弯曲，而总是向内朝太阳弯曲。月球的轨迹更像一个带圆角的十二边形，而不是螺旋线，甚至不是波浪线。不过月球的轨迹非常接近圆形，所以有点难以看出来。这里有一个更简单的轨道例子：一颗行星的卫星，其轨迹始终只朝它的太阳弯曲。看起来这颗假想卫星其实在绕太阳运行，只是在行星绕行时被它稍微推来推去。这种曲线——一个圆在另一个旋转圆上附着并旋转——称为一个

cues.en: though they're usually generated by rolling a circle around another circle, but the curves are the same. It's a fun little bit of geometry depending on how fast the two circles rotate relative to each other and how big they are relative to each other. You get everything from spirals to wiggles to polygons with rounded corners. The faster a moon orbits relative to its planet or the larger the moon's orbit is relative to the planets, the more spirally the trajectory.
cues.zh: 虽然它们通常是通过让一个圆绕另一个圆滚动生成的，但曲线是一样的。这是个有趣的小几何现象，取决于两个圆相对旋转的速度，以及它们相对的大小。从螺旋线、波浪线到圆角多边形，各种形状都有。卫星相对其行星公转得越快，或者卫星轨道相对行星越大，轨迹就越呈螺旋状。

cues.en: The slower the moon moves relative to the planet or the smaller its orbit, the more wobbly or circular trajectory. Looking at a whole table of these trajectories, loops are in the upper right half here and wobbles are in this region. Orbits that never curve outwards are in the remaining sliver. In our case, the sun is about 400 times farther away than the moon and the moon orbits the earth around 13 and a half times for each trip around the sun, once every twenty seven days. The trajectory looks pretty much like a circle. Here's a zoomed in view of what the earth and moon's orbits actually look like exactly to scale, though the earth and moon are not to scale. It does look a lot like the earth and moon are orbiting the sun independently,
cues.zh: 月球相对行星运动得越慢，或轨道越小，轨迹就越摇晃或越接近圆形。看整张轨迹表，环形轨迹在右上这半区，摇摆轨迹在这个区域。从不向外弯曲的轨道在剩下的窄条区域。在我们的情况中，太阳比月球远约400倍；月球每绕太阳一圈，会绕地球约13圈半，即每27天绕地球一圈。这条轨迹看起来几乎就是个圆。这里放大了看地球和月球轨道的实际样子，轨道严格按比例，但地球和月球本身不按比例。看起来确实很像地球和月球在各自独立地绕太阳运行，

cues.en: but side by side, just nudging each other in and out as they go. In order to start having a wobble, the moon would need to orbit about twice as fast as it does, but at the same distance, or be twice as far from the earth and still orbit once per month, or the earth would need to be half as far from the sun and still orbit once per year. In order to start spiraling, the moon would need to orbit about 30 times faster at the same distance or be 30 times farther from the earth and still orbit once per month. But in the real universe, orbital speed and distance can't be adjusted independently. The farther out an object is, the longer it takes to complete an orbit. It turns out the speed matters more, so the moon would have to come closer to Earth where it could orbit faster in order to have a wobbly orbit, one that even curves at all outwards away from the sun. There's a good reason the moon's orbit never curves outwards away from the sun. Due to the distances between the Earth, moon, and sun and their masses, it turns out the sun pulls on the moon with almost twice the force that the earth pulls on the moon. Technically speaking, the moon is outside of the earth's Chebotarov radius where the pull from the earth and sun are equivalent. That means the net force on the moon is always towards the sun and that's why the moon's trajectory never curves outwards towards the earth. There's never a net force that would pull it that way. The force on the moon is always pointing inwards and just gets stronger or weaker over time depending on whether the earth is pulling together with the sun or sideways or against the sun. According to net forces, the moon is primarily orbiting the sun with perturbations from the earth. Except we shouldn't be using net forces because the earth and moon are moving in a circle around the sun, so we need to take into account centrifugal effects. Those effects weaken the sun's relative pull enough that the earth's pull on the moon is stronger. Technically speaking, we say the moon is inside the earth's hill radius or hill sphere, the zone where for practical purposes for objects orbiting along with the earth, the earth's gravitation dominates the sun's. According to the hill radius, the moon orbits the earth. Though technically speaking, the moon doesn't orbit the earth. The moon and the earth both actually orbit the center of mass of the earth moon system. That center of mass is inside the Earth, so it's reasonable to say the moon is orbiting the Earth, but not by much. If the moon were exactly the same but just 40% farther away or if it was in the same place but just 40% more massive, then the Earth Moon center of mass would be outside the Earth, and the Earth and Moon might be better described as a double planet rather than a planet and satellite. Though this would do basically nothing to change the shape of the Moon's trajectory around the Sun. Ultimately, defining whether something is a satellite versus independently orbiting the Sun is actually a really tricky and possibly even futile endeavor. The best way to put it is that the Earth and Moon and Sun interact in a complex gravitational dance that defies simple classification. On the one hand, it looks like the Earth and Moon orbit each other while together orbiting the Sun. And on the other, it looks like the Earth and Moon orbit the Sun side by side, pulling each other back and forth as they go. Both are true from a certain point of view.
cues.zh: 而是并排前进，边走边互相推挤着进出。要想开始摆动，月球需要以相同距离、约两倍于当前的速度绕地球运行，或者在距离翻倍时仍保持每月绕一圈；或者地球离太阳的距离减半，同时仍保持每年绕一圈。要想开始螺旋式运动，月球需要在相同距离上快约 30 倍，或者在距离远 30 倍时仍每月绕一圈。但在真实宇宙中，轨道速度和距离不能独立调整。物体离得越远，完成一圈轨道所需时间越长。结果表明速度影响更大，所以月球必须更靠近地球、从而能绕得更快，才可能有摆动轨道——那种轨道才会向外远离太阳弯曲。月球的轨道从不向远离太阳的方向弯曲，这是有充分理由的。由于地球、月球和太阳之间的距离以及它们的质量，结果太阳对月球的引力几乎是地球对月球引力的两倍。严格来说，月球位于地球的 Chebotarov 半径之外，在这个半径上地球和太阳的引力相当。这意味着月球受到的合力始终指向太阳，所以月球的轨迹从不向外朝地球方向弯曲。从来不存在会把它往那个方向拉的合力。月球所受的力始终指向内侧，只是会随时间变强或变弱，取决于地球是与太阳同向拉、侧向拉，还是反向拉。按照合力来看，月球主要绕太阳运行，并受到地球的摄动。只不过我们不该用合力，因为地球和月球在绕太阳做圆周运动，所以必须考虑离心效应。这些效应削弱了太阳的相对引力，足以让地球对月球的引力更强。严格来说，我们说月球位于地球的 Hill 半径或 Hill 球之内，也就是对随地球一起绕太阳运动的物体而言、地球引力在实际意义上主导太阳引力的区域。按照 Hill 半径，月球绕地球运行。不过严格来说，月球并不绕地球运行。月球和地球实际上都绕地月系统的质心运行。这个质心在地球内部，所以说月球绕地球运行是合理的，但也没多合理。如果月球还是现在这样，只是远 40%，或者位置不变但质量大 40%，那么地月质心就会在地球之外，地球和月球也许更适合描述为双行星，而不是行星和卫星。不过这对月球绕太阳轨迹的形状基本没有影响。最终，判定一个物体是卫星还是独立绕太阳运行，其实非常棘手，甚至可能是徒劳的。最好的说法是，地球、月球和太阳参与一场复杂的引力之舞，无法简单分类。一方面，看起来地球和月球互相绕转，同时一起绕太阳运行；另一方面，看起来地球和月球并排绕太阳运行，边走边互相来回拉扯。从某个角度看，两者都对。

cues.en: Oh, and I definitely wouldn't rely too heavily on the shapes of trajectories to think about orbits. Trajectories can easily be used to mislead you. Like, you might imagine that a point on Earth's equator draws out loops as the Earth spins along its orbit, but because of how fast the Earth is moving around the sun, points on the Earth's surface don't trace out loops, but like the moon, trace out something more like a wobbly circle. Should we then say that each part of the Earth independently orbits the sun? Of course not.
cues.zh: 哦，而且我绝对不会太依赖轨迹的形状来思考轨道问题。轨迹很容易误导你。比如，你可能会想象，地球沿轨道公转时，赤道上的一点会画出一个个环；但由于地球绕太阳运动得很快，地球表面上的点并不会画出环，而是像月球一样，画出更像一个摇晃的圆。那我们是否该说地球的每一部分都独立绕太阳公转？当然不是。
